AGENDA
  SPECIAL GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION MEETING
  (STAFF ACCESS ONLY) GLENDALE WATER & POWER DEPARTMENT
  633 E. Broadway, Room 105 (MSB 105)
  Glendale, CA 91206
 Welcome to the Special Glendale Water & Power Commission Meeting. Meetings are broadcast
 live on cable channel 6 (GTV6) and rebroadcast throughout the week. Call (818) 548-4013 for
 program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City Clerk’s Office.
 Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at
 https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal. If you have any question about
 matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the Glendale Water & Power
 Administration Office at (818) 548-2107 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE COUNCIL CHAMBER.
 In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
 language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
 are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
 requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents related
 to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and
 are public records, will be available for review in the Glendale Water & Power Administration Office,
 141 N. Glendale Ave., Suite 450, Glendale, CA 91206.
 Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
 wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
 Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
 the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
 required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.
  SEPTEMBER 24, 2020 AT 4:00 PM

Due to the evolving situation with the COVID-19 novel coronavirus and health recommendations from
the LA County Health Department, the Special Glendale Water & Power Commission Meeting will be
available to the public electronically.

Due to social distancing requirements, the public will not be able to attend the meeting. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes to practice social distancing.

The meeting can be viewed:
On local cable: Charter Cable Channel 6 and AT&T U-verse Channel 99.
Streaming Online: https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

during the Special Glendale Water & Power Commission Meeting.

MINUTES
  SPECIAL GLENDALE WATER & POWER COMMISSION

  VIA TELECONFERENCE AND MUNICIPAL SERVICE BUILDING
  633 E. Broadway, 1st Floor, Room 105 - Glendale, CA 91206

  Thursday, September 24, 2020, 4:00 PM

1. ROLL CALL
  The meeting was called to order at 4:02 p.m.

  Present: President Kedikian, Commissioners Avanessian, Flanigan, and Jazmadarian

  Absent: Commissioner Lall

2. CONSENT ITEMS
  a. Approval of the August 3, 2020 Meeting Minutes
  The Commission approved the minutes as published.

3. GWP COMMISSION/ STAFF COMMENTS
  Steve Zurn, General Manager of GWP, commented that due to the alarming heatwave and
  longer periods of it, an agenda item addressing potential heatwave impacts would be placed on
  the forecast for the forthcoming GWP Commission Meeting in October 5, 2020.

  Commissioner Avanessian congratulated and welcomed Commissioner Flanigan to the GWP
  Commission.

4. ACTION ITEMS
  a. Recommendation Regarding Three Proposed Clean Energy Programs:
  i. Residential and Commercial Demand Response and Smart Thermostat Program
  and Online Marketplace offered by Franklin Energy Services, LLC
  Mr. Zurn recapped the City Council’s actions and direction to staff on July 23, 2019:
   Approval of the 2019 Integrated Resource Plan.
   Authorized development or “limited notice to proceed” phase for the Glendale
  Energy Center, and
   Shortlisting of clean energy vendors for further negotiations.
  Mr. Zurn also outlined the GWP Implementation of the City Council’s July 23, 2019
  direction to study goals and methods to achieve100% clean energy by 2030.

  Mr. Zurn introduced Ms. Christine Godinez, Principal Assistant City Attorney, who gave
  a high-level overview of staff’s implementation efforts on the Clean Energy Programs.
  Mr. Craig Kuennen, Deputy General Manager/Business Services, presented the
  proposed Franklin Energy Demand Response Program and the proposed Lime Energy
  Commercial Direct Install Program. Mr. Mark Young, Deputy General Manager/Power
  Management, presented the proposed virtual power plant offered by Sunrun, Inc.
  Mr. Kuennen presented estimated costs for the Clean Energy Programs. Mr. Zurn
  1
 introduced Mr. Tony Georgis, NewGen Strategies Solutions, who presented the
estimated rate impacts of the proposed clean energy programs and factors suggesting
that a new Cost of Service Analysis would be beneficial to factor in new data and
information since the 2018 COSA was performed. Mr. Zurn described the next steps,
including GWP recommendation to the City Council and a presentation to the City
Council on October 13, 2020, followed by the implementation of Council-approved
direction.

Messrs. Zurn, Young, Kuennen, and Georgis responded to technical questions by the
Commissioners in reference to the clean energy programs and proposed Electric COSA
Rate Study that will determine the appropriate funding for the clean energy programs.
President Kedikian and the GWP Commissioners commended the GWP staff for the
extensive presentations and preparation of the current clean energy projects/programs.

  1. Motion Providing Recommendations to the City Council and City Council
  Motion to expeditiously move all three proposed clean energy programs (full-
  scale), and for City Council to direct GWP to proceed with the Cost of Service
  (COSA) Analysis.

  Moved by: Commissioner Flanigan
  Seconded by: President Kedikian

  Ayes:  President Kedikian, Commissioner Flanigan
  Noes:  Commissioner Avanessian, Commissioner Jazmadarian
  Absent: Commissioner Lall

  Motion was not passed due to lack of majority vote.

  2. Motion Providing Recommendations to the City Council and City Manager
  to move forward expeditiously with the Franklin and Lime Clean Energy Programs;
  and to proceed with the Sunrun VPP Program on a full-scale basis for a 12-month
  period; to direct GWP staff to negotiate a termination provision or modification
  structure, if necessary, based upon the COSA or initial program results; for GWP
  staff to report back within 12 months from the initiation of the program; to direct
  staff to look at the next phase of the clean energy programs, and to proceed with
  the COSA Analysis.

  Moved by: Commissioner Flanigan
  Seconded by: Commissioner Jazmadarian

  Ayes:  President Kedikian, Commissioners Flanigan, Avanessian, Jazmadarian
  Noes:  n/a
  Absent: Commissioner Lall

  Motion was passed unanimously.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS/SPEAKERS
  Jennifer Pinkerton
  Luis Amezcua (Sierra Club)
  Kate Unger
  Monica Campagna

  2
 5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  None.

6. AGENDA FORECAST
  The Commissioners reviewed and approved the agenda forecast for the October 2020 meeting
  which will include an agenda item, per Mr. Zurn, about to summer heatwave impacts. President
  Kedikian suggested moving the GWP Commission Elections (President and Secretary) to the
  December 7, 2020 Commission meeting. All Commissioners approved.

7. ADJOURNMENT
  Motion to Adjourn:
  Moved by: Commissioner Jazmadarian
  Seconded by: President Kedikian
  Motion Passed.

The meeting was adjourned at 6:32 p.m.
